APPENDIX C 
 
Pro Forma Cost Recovery Agreement

ATTACHMENT A 
 
FORM OF COST RECOVERY AGREEMENT

2 
COST RECOVERY AGREEMENT 
 
This Cost Recovery Agreement (“Agreement”) is made and entered into as of __________ (the 
“Execution Date”) between Horizon West Transmission, LLC (“Horizon West” or “Participating 
Transmission Owner”) and ________________, a [corporation/limited liability company/other] 
organized and existing under the laws of the State/Commonwealth of _____________________ 
(the “Eligible Customer”).  The Eligible Customer is requesting Interconnection service to serve a 
Large Load, as those terms are defined in the Participating Transmission Owner’s tariff. The 
Participating Transmission Owner and Eligible Customer may be referred to herein individually 
as a “Party” or collectively as the “Parties.”  
 
RECITALS 
 
WHEREAS, Participating Transmission Owner is a Non-Load-Serving Entity Participating 
Transmission Owner within the California Independent System Operator, Inc. (“CAISO”) 
Balancing Authority Area that does not provide retail electric service;  
 
WHEREAS, Participating Transmission Owner owns the [Facility Name], which is under 
CAISO’s Operational Control and within the CAISO Controlled Grid; 
 
WHEREAS, Participating Transmission Owner’s Transmission Owner Tariff (the “Tariff”) 
controls the interconnection of load to [Facility Name], subject to compliance with the CAISO 
tariff; 
 
WHEREAS, Eligible Customer is requesting interconnection to Participating Transmission 
Owner’s [Facility Name] for the purpose of serving [describe Large Load requesting service, 
physical location, and MW];  
 
WHEREAS, the Parties have entered into this Agreement to establish the teams and conditions 
for the Interconnection in order to enable the Eligible Customer to serve the Large Load and for 
the Participating Transmission Owner to fully recover from the Eligible Customer the costs 
associated with serving the Large Load. 
 
NOW, THEREFORE, in exchange for good and valuable consideration of the premises and 
mutual covenants herein, the Parties agree as follows: 
 
ARTICLE 1: DEFINITIONS 
 
1.1 
Definitions 
 
Capitalized terms used in this Agreement that are not otherwise defined herein shall have the 
meaning provided in the Participating Transmission Owner Tariff, as may be amended from time-

3 
to-time.  In the event of a difference in a defined term between this Agreement and the definition 
in Module A of the Tariff, the defined term in this Agreement shall control. 
 
1.2 
Annual Required Revenue Commitment 
 
Annual Required Revenue Commitment means the Eligible Customer’s Total Required Revenue 
Commitment divided by twenty (20) years. 
 
1.3 
Cost Recovery Payment 
 
Cost Recovery Payment means the amount the Eligible Customer must pay in addition to the Large 
Load Annual Received Revenue to meet its Annual Required Revenue Commitment. 
 
1.4 
Large Load Annual Received Revenue  
  
Large Load Annual Received Revenue means revenue that is received by the Participating 
Transmission Owner from CAISO through the Access Charges during a specific Rate Year and 
that is directly attributable to the Eligible Customer’s Large Load. 
 
1.5 
Large Load Network Upgrade 
 
Large Load Network Upgrade shall mean any Network Upgrade attributable to an Eligible 
Customer interconnecting on behalf of a Large Load. Large Load Network Upgrades shall be 
specified in the Eligible Customer’s applicable Interconnection Agreement. 
 
1.4 
Monthly Cost Recovery Payment 
 
Monthly Cost Recovery Payment means the Cost Recovery Payment divided by twelve (12) 
months. 
 
1.6 
Total Required Revenue Commitment 
 
Total Required Revenue Commitment means the incremental revenue requirement for any Large 
Load Network Upgrade(s) to serve the Eligible Customer’s Large Load, calculated in accordance 
with Section 3.2. 
 
ARTICLE 2: EFFECTIVE DATE, TERM AND TERMINATION, FILING 
 
2.1 
Effective Date 
 
This Agreement shall be effective as of the date specified herein (“Effective Date”), subject to 
acceptance by FERC. If FERC accepts this Agreement subject to a different effective date,

4 
including in the event the Agreement is filed unexecuted, this Agreement shall become effective 
on the date accepted by FERC. 
 
2.2 
Term and Termination 
 
Unless terminated earlier by mutual consent of the Parties, the term of this Agreement begins on 
the Effective Date and shall continue for twenty (20) years after the final Large Load Network 
Upgrade goes in-service or until, as applicable, the Eligible Customer has satisfied its Total 
Required Revenue Commitment in full pursuant to Article 3 hereof. 
 
2.3 
Filing 
 
The Participating Transmission Owner shall file this Agreement with FERC and/or the appropriate 
Local Regulatory Authority, if applicable. Either Party may request that this Agreement be filed 
unexecuted at FERC. 
 
ARTICLE 3: ELIGIBLE CUSTOMER PAYMENT OBLIGATIONS  
 
3.1 
Performance Obligations 
 
The Eligible Customer shall be responsible for the Total Required Revenue Commitment, as is 
calculated under this Agreement pursuant to the Participating Transmission Owner’s formula rate 
in Appendix III of the Participating Transmission Owner Tariff. The Eligible Customer shall be 
responsible for the timely payment of all applicable invoices assessed herein. This Agreement does 
not relieve Eligible Customer from paying any charges or amounts assessed by the CAISO or any 
other governmental or regulatory authority to the Eligible Customer. 
 
3.2 
Total Required Revenue Commitment 
 
3.2.1 Calculation of Total Required Revenue Commitment 
 
The Total Required Revenue Commitment shall be calculated through the Participating 
Transmission Owner’s formula rate in Appendix III of the Participating Transmission Owner 
Tariff, as further set forth in Section 3.2.2, including the full return on the capital cost, depreciation, 
operations and maintenance, and taxes of the Large Load Network Upgrade(s).   
 
3.2.2 Initial and Adjusted Total Required Revenue Commitment 
 
The initial Total Required Revenue Commitment will be based on the estimated costs of the Large 
Load Network Upgrade(s) and shall be stated in Exhibit A to this Agreement. The Total Required 
Revenue Commitment shall be subject to adjustment by the Participating Transmission Owner the 
to reflect the actual costs of the Large Load Network Upgrade(s), and as necessary to reflect 
changes to the Participating Transmission Owner’s formula rate in Appendix III of its Tariff.

5 
Adjustments to the Total Required Revenue Commitment to reflect actual costs shall be initially 
calculated within one (1) year of the in-service date of the Large Load Network Upgrades, with a 
true-up adjustment as a credit or charge and including interest. For each year thereafter adjustments 
and any true-up shall be provided consistent with the Participating Transmission Owner’s True-up 
Adjustment and Annual Update under the Participating Transmission Owner’s formula rate.  
Interest associated with any initial true-up adjustment will begin to accrue the first day of the 
month following the in-service date of the Large Load Network Upgrades, in accordance with 18 
C.F.R § 35.19a. 
 
3.3 
Required Cost Recovery Payments 
 
Each Rate Year following the Large Load Network Upgrade’s in-service date and continuing 
throughout the term of this Agreement, the Participating Transmission Owner shall:  
 
(a) determine whether the Large Load Annual Received Revenue for that Rate Year meets the 
Annual Required Revenue Commitment; and, if not,  
(b) calculate the Cost Recovery Payment, payable by the Eligible Customer, equal to the 
difference between (i) the Annual Required Revenue Commitment for the applicable Rate 
Year and (ii) the Large Load Annual Received Revenue for that Rate Year, plus any 
applicable interest calculated in accordance with 18 C.F.R § 35.19a.  
 
3.4 
Invoice for Monthly Cost Recovery Payments 
 
Within thirty (30) days of the end of each month of any Rate Year in which a Cost Recovery 
Payment is owed, the Participating Transmission Owner shall invoice the Eligible Customer for 
the Monthly Cost Recovery Payment as determined under Article 8. The Eligible Customer shall 
timely pay such invoice in accordance with Article 8. 
 
3.5 
Treatment of Cost Recovery Payments in the Formula Rate 
 
For each Rate Year during the Term of this Agreement, the Participating Transmission Owner shall 
treat any Cost Recovery Payments required to be paid by the Eligible Customer as a credit against 
the Participating Transmission Owner’s Transmission Revenue Requirement in its formula rate in 
Appendix III of its Tariff, and shall include a separate workpaper in the Participating Transmission 
Owner’s annual informational filing detailing such crediting and rate treatment.  
 
3.6 
Payment in Event of Termination, Cancellation, or Withdrawal 
 
Upon termination, disconnection, suspension, or abandonment of the Large Load project, or should 
the Eligible Customer terminate, cancel, or otherwise withdraw or terminate this Agreement, the 
Interconnection Agreement, or its Interconnection service for any reason, the Eligible Customer 
shall remain obligated to pay to the Participating Transmission Owner all costs incurred or 
committed by the Participating Transmission Owner associated with serving the Large Load,

6 
including Network Upgrades, prior to the effective date of any such termination or change. In the 
event the Eligible Customer fails to make such payment, this Agreement shall not be Terminated 
until such payment is made and payments shall continue to be due under Article 3. The 
Participating Transmission Owner may draw upon the Required Security to satisfy the Eligible 
Customer’s obligations under this Agreement. This Section 3.6 is without prejudice to any other 
remedy available to the Participating Transmission Owner. 
 
ARTICLE 4: Security Requirements 
 
4.1 
Required Security 
 
The Eligible Customer shall provide and maintain financial security in accordance with this Article 
4 (the “Required Security”). The Required Security shall be in an amount equal to the Total 
Required Revenue Commitment and shall take one of the following forms as reasonably acceptable 
to the Participating Transmission Owner:  
 
(a) cash; 
(b) an irrevocable letter of credit issued by a commercial bank that has (i) an office, branch, or 
place of business in the United States where claims can be presented, (ii) assets of at least 
$10 billion, and (iii) a Credit Rating of either “A3” or higher by Moody’s, or (b) “A-” or 
higher by Standard & Poor’s (“S&P”). If a commercial bank is rated by each of Moody’s 
and S&P, the lower rating will be the applicable standard; 
(c) an irrevocable guaranty, provided that the guarantor maintain a senior unsecured credit 
rating of BBB- equivalent by Moody’s, S&P, or Fitch. If the guarantor is rated by one or 
more rating agencies, the lowest rating will be the applicable standard; or 
(d) such other form of security as the Eligible Customer may propose and the Participating 
Transmission Owner, in its sole discretion, determines to be acceptable. 
 
When the amount of Total Required Revenue Commitment is adjusted per Section 3.2.2, the 
amount of Required Security shall be adjusted accordingly. The amount of Required Security may 
be further adjusted in accordance with Sections 4.3 and 4.4. 
 
4.2 
Timing to Provide Required Security 
 
The Eligible Customer shall provide the Required Security within thirty (30) Calendar Days of the 
later of (i) the execution of this Agreement by all parties or (ii) acceptance of this Agreement by 
FERC. Failure to provide the Required Security within such timeframe will result in the Large 
Load Interconnection Application being deemed withdrawn. 
 
4.3 
Annual Reduction of Required Security 
 
The Required Security shall remain with the Participating Transmission Owner for the Term of 
this Agreement. The Participating Transmission Owner will reduce the Required Security

7 
following each Annual Update during the Term of this Agreement to reflect the completed 
payments made by the Eligible Customer pursuant to Article 3 of this Agreement. Any such 
reduced Required Security must be provided in a revised form of irrevocable security otherwise 
meeting the requirements of Section 4.1. 
 
4.4 
Use of Required Security by Participating Transmission Owner 
 
In the event Eligible Customer fails to timely pay any invoice or any other payment due under this 
Agreement, the Participating Transmission Owner shall notify the Eligible Customer in accordance 
with Section 13.4. If the Eligible Customer fails to timely cure and provide such payment within 
five (5) Business Days of receiving such notice, the Participating Transmission Owner shall be 
entitled to draw on the Required Security in the amount of the missed payment, as well as any 
accrued interest charges based on FERC’s regulations at 18 C.F.R § 35.19a. Within twenty (20) 
Business Days of such draw on the Required Security occurring, the Eligible Customer shall be 
required to provide the Participating Transmission Owner with sufficient irrevocable security to 
maintain sufficient Required Security to meet the obligation under Section 4.1 of this Agreement. 
 
4.5 
Term of Required Security 
 
Required Security shall remain in place until the termination of this Agreement. Any Required 
Security provided by Eligible Customer must be kept active, must continue to meet this Article 4’s 
requirements, and must be available to the Participating Transmission Owner in the event that 
Eligible Customer fails to make any payment required under this Agreement.  Any fees or costs 
associated with the provision of the Required Security under this Agreement are the sole 
responsibility of the Eligible Customer. 
 
ARTICLE 5: [RESERVED] 
 
ARTICLE 6: [RESERVED] 
 
ARTICLE 7: CONFIDENTIALITY 
 
7.1 
Confidentiality 
 
During the term of this Agreement and for a period of five (5) years after any termination or 
expiration of this Agreement, each Party shall hold in confidence and not disclose to any person 
any Confidential Information received by a Party (“Receiving Party”) from the other party 
(“Disclosing Party”), and except as Disclosing Party may authorize in writing, a Receiving Party 
who received Confidential Information shall and shall cause its Representatives to: treat and cause 
to be treated as confidential all Confidential Information; not disclose any Confidential 
Information to any third party (other than its Representatives) or make available any reports, 
recommendations, extracts, summaries, analysis, or conclusions based on the Confidential 
Information; use or grant access to Confidential Information only in connection with the

8 
performance of the respective obligations as provided under this Agreement; or make copies of any 
tangible embodiment of Confidential Information only as necessary for the performance of 
respective obligations as provided under this Agreement. 
 
7.2 
Scope 
 
Confidential Information shall include, without limitation, all information relating to a Party’s 
technology, research and development, business affairs, and pricing, and any information supplied 
by a Party to another Party prior to the execution of this Agreement. Information is Confidential 
Information only if it is clearly designated or marked in writing as confidential on the face of the 
document, or, if the information is conveyed orally or by inspection, if the Party providing the 
information orally informs the Party receiving the information that the information is confidential. 
The Parties shall maintain as confidential any information that is provided and identified by a Party 
as Critical Energy/Electric Infrastructure Information (“CEII”), as that term is defined in 18 C.F.R. 
§ 388.113(c).  Such confidentiality will be maintained in accordance with this Article 7. If 
requested by the receiving Party, the disclosing Party shall provide in writing, the basis for 
asserting that the information referred to in this Article warrants confidential treatment, and the 
requesting Party may disclose such writing to the appropriate Governmental Authority. Each Party 
shall be responsible for the costs associated with affording confidential treatment to its 
information. Confidential Information shall not include information that the receiving Party can 
demonstrate:   
 
(a) 
is generally available to the public other than that which is a result of a disclosure by the 
Receiving Party; 
 
(b) 
was in the lawful possession of the Receiving Party on a non-confidential basis before 
receiving it from the Disclosing Party; 
 
(c) 
was supplied to the Receiving Party without restriction by a third party, who, to the 
knowledge of the Receiving Party, after due inquiry, was under no obligation to the 
Disclosing Party to keep such information confidential; 
 
(d) 
was independently developed by the Receiving Party without reference to Confidential 
Information of the Disclosing Party; 
 
(e) 
is, or becomes, publicly known, through no wrongful act or omission of the Receiving 
Party or breach of this Agreement; or 
 
(f) 
is required to be disclosed by any Governmental Authority or is otherwise required to be 
disclosed by law or subpoena or is necessary in any legal proceeding establishing rights 
and obligations under this Agreement.

9 
Information designated as Confidential Information shall no longer be deemed confidential if the 
Party that designated the information as confidential notifies the other Party that it no longer is 
confidential. 
 
7.4 
Release of Confidential Information 
 
No Party shall disclose Confidential Information to any other person, except to its Representatives 
(limited by FERC’s Standards of Conduct requirements) without the prior written consent of the 
disclosing Party.  A receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information to its Representatives 
provided that such Representatives have first been advised of the confidentiality provisions of this 
Article 7.  Notwithstanding the foregoing, a Party providing Confidential Information to a 
Representative shall remain primarily responsible for any release of Confidential Information by 
such Representative in contravention of this Article 7. 
 
7.5 
Rights 
 
Each Party retains all rights, title, and interest in the Confidential Information that it discloses to 
the other Party.  A Party’s disclosure to the other Party of Confidential Information shall not be 
deemed a waiver by such Party or any other person or entity of the right to protect the Confidential 
Information from public disclosure. 
 
7.6 
No Warranties 
 
By providing Confidential Information, neither Party makes any warranties or representations as 
to its accuracy or completeness. 
 
7.7 
Standard of Care 
 
Each Party shall use at least the same standard of care to protect Confidential Information it 
receives as such Party uses to protect its own Confidential Information from unauthorized 
disclosure, publication or dissemination.  Confidential Information may be used solely to fulfill a 
Party’s obligations to the other Party under this Agreement or to comply with Applicable Laws, 
Regulations, and Standards. 
 
7.8 
Order of Disclosure 
 
If a Governmental Authority with the right, power, and apparent authority to do so requests or 
requires a Party, by subpoena, oral deposition, interrogatories, requests for production of 
documents, administrative order, or otherwise, to disclose Confidential Information, that Party 
shall provide the Party that provided the Confidential Information with prompt notice of such 
request(s) or requirement(s) so that the providing Party may seek an appropriate protective order 
or waive compliance with the terms of this Agreement.  Notwithstanding the absence of a 
protective order or agreement, or waiver, the Party that is subjected to the request or order may

10 
disclose such Confidential Information which, in the opinion of its counsel, the Party is legally 
compelled to disclose.  Each Party shall use reasonable efforts to obtain reliable assurance that 
confidential treatment will be accorded to any Confidential Information so furnished. 
 
7.9 
Return or Destruction of Confidential Information 
 
Each Party shall, within ten (10) Business Days of receipt of a written request from the other Party, 
use reasonable efforts to destroy, erase, or delete (with such destruction, erasure and deletion 
certified in writing to the requesting Party) or to return to the requesting Party, without retaining 
copies thereof, any and all written or electronic Confidential Information received from the 
requesting Party, provided that (i) the non-requesting Party shall not be required to purge any 
historical backup media, and (ii) if the non-requesting Party elects to delete, destroy or erase all 
such Confidential Information, it shall certify such deletion, destruction, or erasure to the 
requesting Party in writing. 
 
7.10 
Remedies 
 
Monetary damages would be inadequate to compensate a Party for the other Party’s Breach of its 
obligations under this Article 7; therefore, a Party shall be entitled to injunctive or other equitable 
relief, without bond or proof of damages, if the other Party Breaches or threatens to Breach its 
obligations under this Article 7, and the Party that Breaches or threatens to Breach its obligations 
under this Article 7 shall not plead in defense that there would be an adequate remedy at law.  
Injunctive relief shall not be deemed to be an exclusive remedy for the Breach of this Article 7 and 
shall be in addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity.  The covenants contained 
herein are necessary for the protection of legitimate business interests and are reasonable in scope. 
 
7.11 
Disclosure to Federal or State Commissions or their Staff 
 
Notwithstanding anything in this Article 7 to the contrary, and pursuant to 18 C.F.R. § 1b.20, if 
FERC or its staff, during the course of an investigation or otherwise, requests information from a 
Party that is otherwise required to be maintained in confidence pursuant to this Agreement, such 
Party shall provide the requested information to FERC or its staff, within the time provided for in 
the request for information.  In providing the information to FERC or its staff, the Party must, 
consistent with 18 C.F.R. § 388.112, request that the information be treated as confidential and 
non-public by FERC and its staff and that the information be withheld from public disclosure.  To 
the extent permitted by law, each Party shall notify the other Party prior to the release of the other 
Party’s Confidential Information to FERC or its staff.  A Party shall promptly notify the other Party 
when it is notified by FERC or its staff that a request to release the other Party’s Confidential 
Information has been received by FERC, at which time either of the Parties may respond before 
such information would be made public, pursuant to 18 C.F.R. § 388.112.

11 
7.12 
General Disclosure 
 
Notwithstanding any other provisions of this Article 7, a Party may disclose the Confidential 
Information provided by the other Party to the extent disclosure is:  (i) reasonably deemed by the 
disclosing Party to be required in connection with a dispute between the Parties, or the defense of 
litigation or dispute; (ii) otherwise permitted by written consent of the Party that provided such 
Confidential Information; (iii) necessary to fulfill its obligations to an RTO or ISO or to a regional 
or national reliability organization; or (iv) is required to be disclosed pursuant to any Governmental 
Authority or is otherwise required to be disclosed by law or subpoena.  Prior to any disclosures of 
another Party’s Confidential Information under this Section 7.12, the Disclosing Party shall 
promptly notify the other Party in writing and shall assert confidentiality and cooperate with the 
other Party in seeking to protect the Confidential Information from public disclosure by 
confidentiality agreement, protective order, or other reasonable measures. 
 
7.13 
Audit Rights 
 
Subject to the requirements of confidentiality under Article 7 of this Agreement, (1) the accounts 
and records related to the adjustment provided for in Section 3.2.2 shall be subject to audit for a 
period of twenty-four (24) months following the date the adjustment; and (2) the accounts and 
records related to the determination of whether the Eligible Customer satisfied its Annual Required 
Revenue Commitment shall be subject to audit for a period of twelve (12) months following each 
year’s determination in accordance with this Article 7.  Eligible Customer at its expense shall have 
the right, during normal business hours, and upon prior reasonable notice to the other Parties, to 
audit such accounts and records. Any audit authorized by this Article 7 shall be performed at the 
offices where such accounts and records are maintained and shall be limited to those portions of 
such accounts and records that relate to obligations under this Agreement. 
 
ARTICLE 8: INVOICING AND PAYMENT; TAXES 
 
8.1 
Purpose of Invoicing 
 
Any invoice that is issued pursuant to this Agreement shall be for the purposes set forth in this 
Agreement.   
 
8.2 
Timeliness of Payment 
 
Unless otherwise agreed upon, any invoices issued pursuant to this Agreement shall be rendered 
within thirty (30) Calendar Days of the end of the calendar month in which expenses were incurred 
and shall be due and payable, unless otherwise agreed upon, within thirty (30) Calendar Days of 
receipt of such invoice.  Payment shall be made by electronic transfer or such other means as shall 
cause such payment to be available for the use of the payee.  Interest on unpaid amounts shall be 
determined based on FERC’s regulations at 18 C.F.R § 35.19a.

12 
8.3 
Disputed Invoices 
 
In the event that a Party disputes an invoice, the disputing Party shall pay the invoice in full in 
accordance with Section 8.2 of this Agreement, subject to the refund of any amounts found to have 
been incorrectly invoiced plus interest on such amount from the date of payment to the date of the 
refund at the rate stated in Section 8.2.  In the event of a billing dispute, the disputing Party shall 
provide written notice of the dispute to the billing Party as set out in Section 13.4.  In response to 
the notice, the billing Party will promptly provide all documentation that is reasonably required in 
support of its bill and confer with the disputing Party.  If these good faith efforts fail to resolve the 
issue, the matter may, by mutual agreement of the Parties, be settled through the dispute resolution 
process described in Article 10.   
 
8.4 
Invoice Adjustments 
 
Other than as required by law, regulatory action or metering test adjustments, invoice adjustments 
shall be made within six (6) months of the rendition of the initial invoice. 
 
8.5 
Tax Reimbursement 
 
If, as part of any compensation to be paid under this Agreement, any transaction tax, including, 
but not limited to sales, excise, or similar taxes (other than taxes based on or measured by net 
income) is levied and/or assessed against either Party by any taxing authority on the power and/or 
energy manufactured, generated, produced, converted, sold, purchased, transmitted, interchanged, 
exchanged, exported or imported by the supplying Party to the other Party, then such supplying 
Party shall be fully compensated by the other Party for such direct taxes. 
 
ARTICLE 9: INDEMNITY 
 
To the extent permitted by law, each Party (the “Indemnifying Party”) shall indemnify, save 
harmless, and defend the other Party from and against any losses, liabilities, costs, expenses, suits, 
actions, claims, and all other obligations arising out of injuries or death to persons or damage to 
property (each a “Loss” and each suffered by or asserted by a third party) arising out of, in 
connection with, or resulting from the Indemnifying Party’s (or its Contractor’s) performance or 
non-performance of its obligations under this Agreement; provided, however, that a Party’s 
obligation to indemnify the other Party shall not apply to any Losses arising from the other Party’s 
negligence or intentional misconduct.  Promptly after receipt by a Party entitled to indemnity 
(“Indemnified Party”) of any claim or notice of the commencement of any action, administrative 
or legal proceeding, or investigation as to which the indemnity provided for in this Article 9 may 
apply, the Indemnified Party shall notify the Indemnifying Party of such fact.  Any failure of or 
delay in such notification shall not affect an Indemnifying Party’s indemnification obligation 
unless such failure or delay is materially prejudicial to the Indemnifying Party.

13 
The Indemnifying Party shall, at the Indemnified Party’s option and at the Indemnifying Party’s 
expense, defend the Indemnified Party against any and all suits, actions, or claims arising out of, 
connected with, or resulting from the performance or non-performance by the Indemnifying Party 
or any of its Contractors of its obligations under this Agreement.  The Indemnifying Party shall 
not settle or make a plea with respect to any suit, action or claim without the Indemnified Party’s 
prior written consent. 
 
A Party’s obligations to another Party under this Article 9 shall not be limited in any way by any 
provision of any workers’ compensation, disability benefits, payroll, or other employee benefits 
laws; provided, however, that nothing herein shall limit or restrict any defense a Party may be 
entitled to assert with respect to a Loss, including a defense based on the status of such Party as a 
statutory employer.  EACH PARTY HEREBY SPECIFICALLY AND EXPRESSLY WAIVES 
ANY AND ALL DEFENSES IT MAY HAVE TO AN INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATION TO 
THE OTHER PARTY PURSUANT TO THIS AGREEMENT BASED ON ANY IMMUNITY TO 
WHICH SUCH PARTY MAY BE ENTITLED UNDER ANY WORKERS’ COMPENSATION, 
DISABILITY BENEFITS, PAYROLL, OR EMPLOYEE BENEFITS LAWS. 
 
For the purposes of this Article 9 only, the term “Party” shall include the Party’s Affiliates and the 
directors, officers, employees, and agents of the Party and its Affiliates. 
 
ARTICLE 10: DISPUTES 
 
10.1 
Dispute Resolution 
 
The Parties shall attempt, in good faith, to resolve or cure any dispute, controversy or claim (a 
“Dispute”) before initiating any formal legal action at law or in equity to resolve the same. If either 
Party believes that a Dispute has arisen, such Party shall give written notice thereof to the other 
Party, which notice shall describe in reasonable detail the basis and specifics of the claimed Dispute 
(the “Dispute Notice”). Within five (5) Business Days after delivery of the Dispute Notice, each 
Party shall appoint a senior level executive.  Each designated executive shall meet (in person or 
via telephone) to discuss and attempt to resolve or cure such Dispute.  
 
Each senior level executive shall negotiate for a reasonable period of time to settle the Dispute 
after the Dispute Notice is referred to them; provided that such reasonable period shall not, unless 
otherwise agreed by the Parties in writing, exceed twenty (20) Business Days from the time of 
receipt of the Dispute Notice by the senior level executive of each Party, or longer period of time 
if agreed to by the Parties.  Notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein, in no event will the 
executive officer to whom the matter is referred be a person who is an attorney without the express 
written permission of the chief legal counsel of the other Party. 
 
If the Dispute has not been resolved pursuant to this Section 10.1 within thirty (30) Business Days 
from the time of receipt of the Dispute Notice by the applicable individual, either Party may

14 
proceed to take any and all actions available to it under this Agreement to resolve such dispute and 
to obtain any remedies available under this Agreement. 
 
10.2 
Not Usable As Evidence 
 
Nothing said or disclosed, nor any document produced, in the course of any negotiations, 
conferences and discussion in connection with efforts to settle a Dispute that is not otherwise 
independently discoverable shall be offered or received as evidence or used for impeachment or 
for any other purposes in any suit, but shall be considered to have been disclosed for settlement 
purposes. 
 
ARTICLE 11: BREACH AND DEFAULT 
 
11.1 
General 
 
A Party shall be considered in default of this Agreement (“Default”) if it fails to cure a Breach in 
accordance with the terms of this Section 11.1.  A breach (“Breach”) shall mean the failure of a 
Party to perform or observe any material term or condition of this Agreement; provided that no 
Breach shall exist where such failure to discharge an obligation (other than the payment of money) 
is the result of Force Majeure as defined in this Agreement or the result of an act or omission by 
the other Party. Upon a Breach, the non-breaching Party shall give written notice of such Breach 
to the breaching Party.  The breaching Party shall have thirty (30) Calendar Days from receipt of 
the Breach notice within which to cure such Breach; provided however, if such Breach is not 
capable of cure within thirty (30) Calendar Days, the breaching Party shall commence such cure 
within thirty (30) Calendar Days after notice and continuously and diligently complete such cure 
within ninety (90) Calendar Days from receipt of the Breach notice; and, if cured within such time, 
the Breach specified in such notice shall cease to exist. 
 
11.2 
Consequence of Default 
 
In the event of Default, Eligible Customer shall promptly pay any remaining Total Required 
Revenue Commitment owed under this Agreement.  In the event that Eligible Customer does not 
promptly such amount, the Participating Transmission Owner may draw on the Required Security. 
This payment or draw on the Required Security does not limit any and all rights and remedies 
available to the non-defaulting Parties allowed by law with respect to such default or collecting all 
amounts owed under this Agreement. The Defaulting Party shall indemnify non-Defaulting Parties 
for reasonable costs, attorney fees and/or expenses incurred with respect to a default or collecting 
all amounts owed, including, as applicable, any tax gross-up obligations under this Agreement.

15 
ARTICLE 12: GOVERNMENTAL AUTHORITIES; AMENDMENT 
 
12.1 
Governmental Authorities 
 
This Agreement is made subject to the jurisdiction of FERC and any Local Regulatory Authority 
having jurisdiction over the rates, terms and conditions, or services provided under this Agreement. 
Nothing in this Agreement shall limit the rights of the Parties or of FERC under Sections 205 and
